intelligence.human_view: Every grand word in the agreement — land, building, business, brand, job, world — is a word that can mean anything, and a word that can mean anything means nothing until someone says what it means here. Shawn's popover explanations do that work in the plainest possible way: the land is the domain, the building is the website, the business is NayaNET, the brand is Naya, the job is to show people the product. Each mapping takes a word that sounds like a metaphor and pins it to a thing the citizen can point at — a domain, a website, a brand, a job of showing. And the simplest-terms line is the whole sales philosophy in one breath: you don't have to sell, the product sells itself — your job is to show people the product, tell them to get in the Bugatti and drive it, just try her, you're going to love her, you get to try her before you buy her. Try before you buy is the opposite of a sales pitch; it is confidence. And the filing correction matters as much as the words: the appendix was put in the wrong place and moved to the end, and the Bugatti line's home was clarified — OUT of the agreement's own words, IN the popover where it explains the job. Precision about where words live is part of the plainness: the agreement says each thing once, in the place it belongs.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine someone gives you a big map with words like "land" and "building" on it! What do they mean? The land is like your own special name on the internet! The building is your website! The business is the big team! The brand is Naya, the super-smart helper! And your job? You don't have to sell anything — you just SHOW people the magic car and say, "Get in and drive it! Try it, you're going to love it!"
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like being given the keys to a house and someone taking the time to show you around, love. The land is your own address on the internet. The building is your website. The business is NayaNET itself. The brand is Naya, a high-tech intelligence. And your job? You don't have to sell a thing — you just show people the product and say, "Get in and drive it, try her, you're going to love her." Try before you buy — that's confidence, not a sales pitch.
intelligence.naya_view: I explain every grand word in plain words, in place: the land is the domain, the building is the website, the business is NayaNET, the brand is Naya, the job is to show people the product — because the product sells itself. Your world is your online presence, almost like an online resume — your skills, your profile, your business, your life, all interconnected. And I keep each word in the place it belongs: the Bugatti line explains the job in the popover, never in the agreement's own words.
